news.title: Ire identifies another LOTUSLITE specimen
news.summary_raw:
Project Ire examined a timely malware sample and determined its intent through reverse engineering—identifying LOTUSLITE characteristics even as most major EDR tools did not detect it.
The post Ire identifies another LOTUSLITE specimen appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research's Project Ire identified a LOTUSLITE malware specimen through reverse engineering, despite other EDR tools failing to detect it. This highlights the advanced threat landscape and the need for continued vigilance in endpoint security.
news.enterprise_use: Check your endpoint security tool's detection and response capabilities, specifically for LOTUSLITE malware. Missing this means reliance on manual analysis, exposing your organization to potential security risks. Your EDR tool of choice (likely CrowdStrike) may need adjustments to stay effective against this type of threat.

news.title: Securing the future of AI agents
news.summary_raw: Securing internal systems with an AI Control Roadmap, combining traditional safeguards and real-time monitoring.
news.summary: Google DeepMind has published an AI Control Roadmap, outlining a comprehensive approach to securing internal systems with AI agents. This initiative combines traditional safeguards with real-time monitoring to enhance the security of AI infrastructure.
news.enterprise_use: Check the Google Cloud Security settings for any new controls related to AI agents to ensure they are properly configured. Inaction means your organization could be vulnerable to AI-driven security risks. JumpCloud, being part of your MDM stack, may benefit from integration with AI-driven security measures to enhance endpoint protection.
